badge.text: Control your PC's colours from your phone

hero.lead: Syntra is a Windows colour app for gamers. It changes what your monitor shows — never the game.

features.title: Saturation to 300%
features.text: Go past your driver's limit. Plus vibrance, brightness, contrast, gamma, temperature, shadows and highlights.

features.title: Hue changer
features.text: Shift colours on the whole screen — or on one app, like Discord, on any monitor.

features.title: Crosshair overlay
features.text: GTA PvP and more presets, your own colours and outlines, size from 0.01× to 50×.

features.title: Resolution switcher
features.text: Every mode your screen supports and stretched 4:3 — with a 15-second safety undo.

features.title: Monitor controls
features.text: Your monitor's real brightness and contrast, plus low blue light for late sessions.

features.title: Game profiles
features.text: A look for each game, on when it's in front, put back when you leave.

features.title: Phone control
features.text: Drag a slider on your phone and your PC follows live, from anywhere.

features.title: Make it yours
features.text: Eight themes, your accent colour, a background picture, a see-through window.

features.title: Updates itself
features.text: Installs in a click, adds a shortcut, and keeps itself on the newest version.

safe.title: No memory reading
safe.text: Syntra never reads a game's memory.

safe.title: No file changes
safe.text: It never changes a game's files.

safe.title: No injection
safe.text: It never puts code into a game or any other program.

safe.title: No drivers
safe.text: It installs no driver. Nothing runs at kernel level.

safe.title: No admin needed
safe.text: It runs as you. The repair button asks Windows first.

steps: Open Syntra on your PC and sign in.
Scan the QR code in Settings → Control from anywhere.
Sign in on your phone and drag. Your screen follows.

faq.a: Syntra never touches a game — no memory reading, no injection, no file changes. It only changes what Windows sends to your monitor. Every game has its own rules, so it's always your job to check them.

No. It only changes the colours your PC sends, like a very colourful picture. Normal LCD monitors don't get burn-in. On OLED, watch out for any bright image that stays in one spot for hours — like a crosshair.

faq.q: Does it work with NVIDIA and AMD?
faq.a: Yes. On NVIDIA, Syntra also uses your driver's own Digital Vibrance. Everything else works on any graphics card.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
faq.a: Syntra is new and not code-signed yet. Click More info, then Run anyway. You can check your copy is official in Settings → Verify this copy.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything else?
faq.a: No. One file. No .NET, no Python, no installer — it sets itself up and adds a shortcut.
